messages.subject: problem
parts:
Hello All,
I have a question about SEM in lavaan. 
I have 735 plots for biomass, plant species number, plant species richness and cover (%), also I have for each plot slope, elevation, direction and X, Y, but I have in 175 plots soil samples (some chemical soil parameters such as N, EC, pH, P, OM, CACO3, silt, clay, sand, soil depth). 
I want to know links between species richness with plant biomass, topography and soil parameters.
Since the number of plant (735 plots) and soil samples (175 soil samples) are not equal, 
Can I use the SEM to reach the mechanisms linking productivity and plant species richness?

Best Regards,
Anvar,

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: problem
parts:
This sounds like a conceptual question, not about any particular software package.  SEMNET is more appropriate for general SEM questions:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

If the 175 soil samples came from 175 of the 735 plots that your plant samples came from, then you should still be able to fit a model to all variables, using FIML to utilize all available information.  In the ?lavaan help page, you can see how to specify that using the "missing" argument.  But it is hard to tell whether that is actually the case without knowing what model you want to fit.  "Links" sounds like you are just interested in correlations between different variables, but perhaps you have a more complicated path model in mind.  When you post on SEMNET, perhaps include a link or attachment of a path diagram that explains your model.
